claims.summary: For any odd-dimensional root curve n>=3 over any odd-characteristic field, let c=(n-3)/2,kappa=O(cH),A0=[H-BP0],MA0=0. For bulk d, a=d-c,r=a modM,t=vp(a), put Lambda_r=kappa*A0^r and form the full residue pairing Psi_(r,t) on H0(Lambda_r) times H0(K*Lambda_r^-1), with entries Res_P0(omega/T^(p^t)). If H0(Lambda_r)=0 or Psi is nonsingular, original Vd is normal at a moving mark and hence generically. Over F_(p^e), all central classes share a stable Cartier period dividing e*p^b*lcm(p^(ej)-1,j1..G), G=(n-1)/2,p^b>=G minimal, afterG iterates. This is sufficient, not a complete table.

At every N<=p^s the actual moving kernel bundle modulo u^N has at least h* independent primitive sections, so no uniform ordinary lifting depth kills all sections. The depth conclusion extends to finite smooth-reduction root families with varying moduli via the lifted torsion section. This is not actual generic nonnormality or an obstruction to all algorithms.
claims.assessment: Working uniform counterfamily. RR gives h0((c+1)H)-B=h*. Low-degree dual sections annihilate the first cup image. Torsion and Frobenius identify the high-degree bundle modulo u^N with the positive low-degree moving family; its finite free section module specializes injectively. The sole medium reviewer passed primitive-section, finite-palette and varying-family arguments without corrections. The n3 boundary h*=0 is an explicit scope control.
claims.rationale: Rules out completing the inventory by enlarging finite central first-cup tables or imposing a uniform lifting-depth cap, even after the degree-offset Frobenius extraction. It preserves the preceding sparse normality theorem and requires genuinely higher relative lifting or another certificate architecture.
